newsitem.title: SPAIN: BA, American to take five pct stakes in Iberia.
newsitem.headline: BA, American to take five pct stakes in Iberia.

text.p: Spain's state holding company SEPI, which controls flag carrier Iberia, said in an interview published on Sunday that British Airways and American Airlines would take five percent stakes in the Spanish carrier.

Following the announcement of preliminary agreements with BA and American on an alliance, SEPI said the two airlines would take symbolic stakes in Iberia at the end of the year, kicking off the Spanish state airline's privatisation process.

"At the end of this year we will start the process with the symbolic sale of five percent to American and British," SEPI's chairman Pedro Ferreras said in an interview published by the newspaper El Periodico.
In a separate interview, Iberia said the government would then make preparations to sell around 30 percent to industrial and financial groups.
"The next step will be to place around 30 percent between industrial and financial groups," Ferreras said in an interview published in the newspaper El Mundo.
"Another 10 percent will be in the hands of workers, and the rest will be launched on the bourse," he added.
Industry Minister Josep Pique said earlier in the week the government aimed to float around 50 percent of Iberia by the end of 1999.
Ferreras said the government was in no hurry to privatise the airline.
"We hope that in 1999 Iberia's results will be equivalent to those at Endesa, Repsol or Telefonica, and after that we can privatise the airline," he told El Periodico.
Ferreras said the new alliance would prompt a fall in tariffs. "The primary beneficiary of this deal will be the consumer," he said.
Iberia ended 1996 with a profit of 3.5 billion pesetas and said in February it expected to make a profit of 11 billion pesetas for this year.
